candidates.name: Tricuspid Atresia
support_spans: severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice
candidates.why: The presence of a hypoplastic left ventricle and reduced mitral valve orifice suggests tricuspid atresia.

candidates.name: Ebstein's Anomaly
support_spans: severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
severe tricuspid regurgitation
candidates.why: The combination of right atrial and ventricular dilation with severe tricuspid regurgitation is consistent with Ebstein's anomaly.

candidates.name: Pulmonary Atresia with Intact Ventricular Septum
support_spans: two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle
contradict_spans: a 6 mm muscular interventricular defect in the dorsal septum
candidates.why: The presence of two great vessels arising from the right ventricle suggests pulmonary atresia, but the presence of a ventricular septal defect argues against this diagnosis.

key_evidence_spans: severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle

candidates.name: Tricuspid Atresia
support_spans: severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice
contradict_spans: a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur
candidates.why: The presence of severe right atrial and ventricular dilation along with a hypoplastic left ventricle suggests a condition where the right side of the heart is overburdened, possibly due to tricuspid atresia.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be overlooked due to the complexity of the cardiac defects and the presence of multiple septal defects.

candidates.name: Double Outlet Right Ventricle
support_spans: two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle
differentiated by coronary arteries from one vessel and by left and right pulmonary arteries from the other
contradict_spans: a 16 mm interatrial defect in the upper septum
candidates.why: The presence of two great vessels arising from the right ventricle is highly suggestive of double outlet right ventricle, a condition where both the aorta and pulmonary artery originate from the right ventricle.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis requires specific imaging findings and may be missed if not considered in the differential diagnosis.

contradict_spans: a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice
candidates.why: The presence of severe tricuspid regurgitation and cyanosis suggests a condition affecting the tricuspid valve, such as Ebstein's anomaly.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be overlooked due to the presence of other cardiac defects and the complexity of the clinical presentation.
